顺浓度 + 要蛋白 → 协助扩散；逆浓度 + 耗能 → 主动运输: Down the gradient + needs a protein → facilitated diffusion; against the gradient + uses energy → active transport
同一片细胞膜，为什么氧能自己穿过去、葡萄糖要好几个蛋白帮忙、K⁺ 还能逆着浓度往: It's the same cell membrane. Why can oxygen cross by itself, glucose needs proteins to help, and K⁺ can even move inward against its concentration?
顺浓度、不要蛋白、不耗能: Down the gradient, no protein, no energy
顺浓度、要转运蛋白: Down the gradient, needs a transport protein
逆浓度、要载体蛋白、耗 ATP: Against the gradient, needs a carrier protein, uses ATP
大分子走囊泡、靠膜流动性: Large molecules travel in vesicles, relying on membrane fluidity
一个动物细胞：细胞膜、细胞质、细胞核；细胞内一侧的浓度设为 100: An animal cell: cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus; the concentration inside the cell is set to 100
磷脂双分子层与转运蛋白，物质的分子从这里过；上方是细胞外: Phospholipid bilayer and transport proteins, where molecules cross; outside the cell is above
膜内陷包住大分子形成囊泡；囊泡与膜融合把大分子放出: The membrane folds in around a large molecule to form a vesicle; a vesicle fuses with the membrane to release a large molecule
氧为什么能自己穿过细胞膜？往哪边走又由什么定？: Why can oxygen cross the cell membrane by itself? And what decides which way it goes?
把外界浓度从 120 拖到 0，看氧往哪边走: Drag the outside concentration from 120 to 0 and see which way oxygen goes
外界浓度 120（外面比里面多）时，氧净进入细胞，读数 +5.0（肺泡一侧）；拖: At an outside concentration of 120 (more outside than in), oxygen moves into the cell on net, reading +5.0 (the alveolar side); dragged to 0, oxygen moves out instead, reading −25.0. When the direction reverses, the textbook's matching scene is carbon dioxide diffusing out of cells in tissues. Transport proteins and energy supply have no effect on oxygen
顺浓度梯度 · 不耗能: Down the concentration gradient · no energy
氧和二氧化碳很容易自由地通过细胞膜的磷脂双分子层。: Oxygen and carbon dioxide pass very easily and freely through the phospholipid bilayer of the cell membrane.
肺泡一侧氧浓度高，氧扩散进细胞；组织一侧二氧化碳浓度高，二氧化碳扩散出细胞——同: On the alveolar side oxygen concentration is high, so oxygen diffuses into cells; on the tissue side carbon dioxide concentration is high, so it diffuses out: the same mode, two directions.
甘油、乙醇、苯等脂溶性小分子也走自由扩散。: Small fat-soluble molecules such as glycerol, ethanol and benzene also move by simple diffusion.
去掉这一步：会以为物质过膜都要蛋白——与协助扩散的分界就丢了。: Skip this step and students think everything needs a protein to cross the membrane, losing the boundary with facilitated diffusion.
判断：自由扩散需要转运蛋白——错。: True or false: simple diffusion needs a transport protein. False.
自由扩散顺浓度梯度进行，不需要转运蛋白、不消耗能量；方向由浓度差决定，两个方向都: Simple diffusion goes down the concentration gradient without transport proteins or energy; its direction is set by the concentration difference, and it can go either way.
葡萄糖也是小分子，它能不能自己穿过去？: Glucose is a small molecule too. Can it cross by itself?
把转运蛋白从 10 个拖到 0，看葡萄糖还能不能进: Drag the transport proteins from 10 to 0 and see whether glucose can still get in
转运蛋白拖到 0：葡萄糖净流量从 +6.0 掉到 0.0，分子全挤在膜外进不去；: With transport proteins at 0, glucose's net flux drops from +6.0 to 0.0 and the molecules crowd outside the membrane, unable to enter; switch the substance to oxygen and drag the concentration to 60, and changing proteins has no effect on oxygen (still −10.0)
要转运蛋白 · 不耗能: Needs a transport protein · no energy
细胞膜不是筛子：它对物质的进出有选择（课标 2.1.1 选择透过性）。: The cell membrane isn't a sieve: it is selective about what enters and leaves (curriculum standard 2.1.1, selective permeability).
不带电荷的无机小分子、脂溶性的有机小分子能自由扩散。: Small uncharged inorganic molecules and small fat-soluble organic molecules can diffuse freely.
离子和葡萄糖、氨基酸这样的小分子有机物必须借助转运蛋白。: Ions and small organic molecules such as glucose and amino acids must rely on transport proteins.
去掉这一步：会以为小分子都能自由扩散，把葡萄糖归错类。: Skip this step and students think all small molecules diffuse freely, misclassifying glucose.
配套答案：相对分子质量小的物质或离子都可以通过自由扩散进入细胞内——错（p.72: Teacher's guide answer: substances with low relative molecular mass, or ions, can all enter the cell by simple diffusion. False (p.72, exercise 1(1)).
细胞膜具有选择透过性：离子和葡萄糖、氨基酸等小分子有机物不能自由通过磷脂双分子层: The cell membrane is selectively permeable: ions and small organic molecules such as glucose and amino acids can't pass freely through the phospholipid bilayer and must rely on transport proteins.
蛋白多了，葡萄糖就进得快吗？它要不要能量？: With more proteins, does glucose get in faster? Does it need energy?
把转运蛋白从 5 个加到 10 个，比一比净流量: Increase the transport proteins from 5 to 10 and compare the net flux
同样的浓度差，蛋白从 5 个加到 10 个，净流量从 +3.0 涨到 +6.0；: With the same concentration difference, going from 5 to 10 proteins raises the net flux from +3.0 to +6.0; switch to oxygen and the number of proteins makes no difference
J ∝（外界浓度 − 细胞内浓度）× 转运蛋白数量: J ∝ (outside concentration − inside concentration) × number of transport proteins
协助扩散借助膜上的转运蛋白，顺浓度梯度进行。: Facilitated diffusion uses transport proteins in the membrane and goes down the concentration gradient.
浓度差越大越快；转运蛋白越多也越快（两个系数只为让两条线分得开，不代表葡萄糖真的: The larger the concentration difference, the faster; more transport proteins also make it faster (the two coefficients only keep the lines apart; they don't mean glucose is really faster than oxygen).
红细胞吸收葡萄糖就是协助扩散（要蛋白，但不耗能）；这一步也不用能量——关掉供能，: Red blood cells take up glucose by facilitated diffusion (protein needed, but no energy); this step doesn't use energy either: turn off the energy supply and glucose's flux doesn't change at all.
去掉这一步：会以为要蛋白就是主动运输，把被动与主动的分界弄反。: Skip this step and students think "needs a protein" means active transport, flipping the passive/active boundary.
葡萄糖进入红细胞需要借助转运蛋白，但不消耗能量，属于协助扩散（p.72 练习 2: Glucose entering red blood cells needs a transport protein but no energy, so it's facilitated diffusion (p.72, exercise 2, option C).
协助扩散：借助转运蛋白、顺浓度梯度、不消耗能量；某些物质的运输速率还与转运蛋白的: Facilitated diffusion: uses transport proteins, goes down the concentration gradient, uses no energy; for some substances the rate also depends on the number of transport proteins.
转运蛋白只有一种吗？两种蛋白有什么不一样？: Is there only one kind of transport protein? How do the two kinds differ?
点一下膜上的转运蛋白，看它的形状: Tap a transport protein on the membrane to see its shape
通道蛋白是四根柱子围成的孔，分子穿过时不与它结合；载体蛋白像一把夹子，要先与分子: A channel protein is a pore ringed by four pillars, and molecules pass through without binding to it; a carrier protein works like a clamp, first binding the molecule and then changing its own shape to deliver it to the other side
转运蛋白 = 载体蛋白 + 通道蛋白: Transport proteins = carrier proteins + channel proteins
转运蛋白分载体蛋白和通道蛋白两类。: Transport proteins come in two kinds: carrier proteins and channel proteins.
载体蛋白只容许与自身结合部位相适应的分子通过，每次转运都要改变构象。: A carrier protein only lets through molecules that fit its binding site, and changes shape every time it transports one.
通道蛋白只容许大小和电荷相宜的分子通过，不需要与分子结合；钾离子通道是典型。: A channel protein only lets through molecules of suitable size and charge without binding them; potassium channels are a classic example.
去掉这一步：会把「载体」和「通道」当同一个东西，遇到主动运输（要载体）就说不清。: Skip this step and students treat "carrier" and "channel" as the same thing, unable to explain active transport (which needs a carrier).
配套答案：载体蛋白和通道蛋白的转运机制一样——错（p.67 练习 1（3））。: Teacher's guide answer: carrier proteins and channel proteins work the same way. False (p.67, exercise 1(3)).
转运蛋白分载体蛋白和通道蛋白：载体要与分子结合并改变构象，通道只让大小和电荷相宜: Transport proteins are carriers and channels: carriers bind the molecule and change shape; channels just let molecules of suitable size and charge through without binding.
细胞里的 K⁺ 比外面多得多（教材：红细胞内比血浆高 30 倍），为什么还能继续: There's far more K⁺ inside the cell than outside (textbook: 30 times higher in red blood cells than in plasma). Why can it keep taking more in?
把供能断掉，看 K⁺ 还进不进得去: Cut off the energy supply and see whether K⁺ still gets in
有 ATP 时：外界浓度只有 20（远低于细胞内的 100），K⁺ 仍净流入，读: With ATP: the outside concentration is only 20 (far below 100 inside), yet K⁺ still moves in on net, reading +5.2, mode "active transport", energy "uses ATP". Cut the energy and the reading becomes −0.8, the direction flips to "leaving the cell", and the mode and energy switch to "facilitated diffusion · channel protein" and "none": the pump stops and only leakage through channels remains
J = 泵（耗 ATP）− 漏（顺浓度）: J = pump (uses ATP) − leak (down the gradient)
逆浓度梯度 · 要载体蛋白 · 耗能: Against the gradient · needs a carrier protein · uses energy
人红细胞内 K⁺ 浓度比血浆高 30 倍、轮藻高 63 倍、甲状腺滤泡上皮细胞的: Human red blood cells hold 30 times more K⁺ than plasma, Chara cells 63 times more, and thyroid follicle cells 20–25 times more iodine than blood, all built up against the concentration gradient.
载体蛋白与离子结合后，在能量推动下改变构象，把离子送到另一侧。: Once a carrier protein binds an ion, energy drives it to change shape and deliver the ion to the other side.
主动运输让细胞按需要吸收、排出废物和有害物质。: Active transport lets cells take in what they need and expel waste and harmful substances.
去掉这一步：「耗能」就是一句空话，学生不知道能量断了会发生什么。: Skip this step and "uses energy" is an empty phrase; students don't know what happens when energy is cut.
配套答案：物质逆浓度梯度跨膜运输时，既要消耗能量，也要借助载体蛋白——对（p.7: Teacher's guide answer: moving a substance across a membrane against its concentration gradient requires both energy and a carrier protein. True (p.72, exercise 1(4)).
主动运输：逆浓度梯度、需要载体蛋白、消耗 ATP。断了能量，泵停，剩下的只是 K: Active transport: against the concentration gradient, needs carrier proteins, uses ATP. Cut the energy and the pump stops; what remains is K⁺ leaking down its gradient through channels, which is facilitated diffusion, not active transport.
蛋白质这么大，转运蛋白运不了，它怎么进出细胞？: Proteins are so large that transport proteins can't carry them. How do they get in and out of cells?
现在是「大分子（胞吞）」，把物质切到「分泌蛋白（胞吐）」，看方向反过来: It's currently "Large molecule (endocytosis)". Switch the substance to "Secreted protein (exocytosis)" and watch the direction reverse
大分子（胞吞）：膜内陷成小囊把它包住，小囊分离成囊泡进入细胞，读数 +3.0；切: Large molecule (endocytosis): the membrane folds in to wrap it in a pouch that pinches off as a vesicle into the cell, reading +3.0; switch to secreted protein (exocytosis): a vesicle moves to the membrane and fuses with it, releasing the large molecule, reading −3.0. In both cases the reading doesn't depend on outside concentration or the number of transport proteins
大分子 ⇄ 囊泡（膜内陷 / 膜融合）: Large molecule ⇄ vesicle (membrane infolding / membrane fusion)
依赖膜的流动性 · 也得耗能: Relies on membrane fluidity · also uses energy
转运蛋白对蛋白质和多糖这样的大分子无能为力。: Transport proteins can't handle large molecules such as proteins and polysaccharides.
胞吞时大分子先与膜上蛋白质结合，膜内陷形成小囊，小囊分离成囊泡进入细胞。: In endocytosis a large molecule first binds to a membrane protein, the membrane folds in to form a pouch, and the pouch pinches off as a vesicle into the cell.
胞吐时囊泡移动到细胞膜处融合，把大分子排出细胞。: In exocytosis a vesicle moves to the cell membrane and fuses with it, releasing the large molecule outside.
去掉这一步：会以为胞吞胞吐是主动运输的一种，讲不出它靠的是膜的形状变化。: Skip this step and students think endocytosis and exocytosis are a kind of active transport, unable to say they rely on the membrane changing shape.
细胞内的生物大分子（如胃蛋白酶原）运出细胞的方式是胞吐（p.72 练习 3）。: Large biological molecules inside the cell (such as pepsinogen) leave the cell by exocytosis (p.72, exercise 3).
胞吞胞吐：大分子先与膜上的蛋白质结合，靠膜内陷成囊泡（胞吞，向内）/ 囊泡与膜融: Endocytosis and exocytosis: large molecules first bind to membrane proteins and enter or leave by the membrane folding in to form vesicles (endocytosis, inward) / vesicles fusing with the membrane (exocytosis, outward); this relies on membrane fluidity and also uses energy.
四种方式摆在一起，差在哪几件事？: Put the four modes side by side. In which ways do they differ?
拖动视角，把细胞、细胞膜、囊泡三个单元看一遍: Drag the view to look over the three units: cell, membrane and vesicle
细胞、细胞膜、囊泡三样都在画面里；换物质、拖浓度、拖蛋白、拨供能，读数与曲线跟着: Cell, membrane and vesicle are all on screen; change the substance, concentration, proteins or energy supply and the readings and curve follow, so you can point out on the spot "down or against the gradient, protein or not, energy or not"
顺浓度 → 被动；逆浓度 → 主动: Down the gradient → passive; against the gradient → active
判断方式先问两件事：顺还是逆浓度、耗不耗能。: To identify the mode, ask two things first: down or against the gradient, and does it use energy.
再看要不要转运蛋白、要哪一种（载体还是通道）。: Then ask whether a transport protein is needed, and which kind (carrier or channel).
水是唯一两种被动方式都走的物质：自由扩散 + 水通道蛋白的协助扩散。: Water is the only substance that uses both passive modes: simple diffusion + facilitated diffusion through aquaporins.
去掉这一步：四种方式各自都对，合起来却说不出一张对照表。: Skip this step and students get each of the four modes right but can't put them into one comparison table.
被动运输包括自由扩散与协助扩散，两者都顺浓度、都不耗能；主动运输逆浓度、耗能、要: Passive transport includes simple and facilitated diffusion, both down the gradient and neither using energy; active transport goes against the gradient, uses energy and needs carrier proteins.
顺浓度 + 不要蛋白 → 自由扩散；顺浓度 + 要蛋白 → 协助扩散；逆浓度 +: Down the gradient + no protein → simple diffusion; down the gradient + protein → facilitated diffusion; against the gradient + carrier protein + energy → active transport; large molecules → endocytosis/exocytosis.
A9 七条（p.73）、A5.1、A6.3、A7.2: A9 seven items (p.73), A5.1, A6.3, A7.2
考核：让 K⁺ 在「外面比里面少」的情况下继续往细胞里走: Assessment: keep K⁺ moving into the cell even when there's less outside than inside
切到 K⁺、供能打开、外界浓度降到 50 以下、载体蛋白加到 7 个以上，让净流: Switch to K⁺, turn the energy supply on, lower the outside concentration below 50, add at least 7 carrier proteins, so the net flux falls within 3.5–5.5, and hold for 15 seconds
达标横幅；中途会有一次供能断开，方向翻成排出，要把供能拨回来再调一次: Pass banner; partway through the energy supply will be cut once and the direction flips to outward, so switch the energy back on and adjust again
主动运输的方向是逆浓度，不是顺浓度。: Active transport goes against the gradient, not down it.
没有 ATP 就没有主动运输，只剩顺浓度的漏。: Without ATP there's no active transport, only leakage down the gradient.
没有载体蛋白也没有主动运输。: Without carrier proteins there's no active transport either.
考核没有新内容：前面五步都用得上。: Nothing new in the assessment: you'll use the earlier five steps.
主动运输的两个条件：载体蛋白 + 能量；方向：逆浓度梯度。: Two conditions for active transport: carrier proteins + energy; direction: against the concentration gradient.
考核没有新结论：主动运输要同时满足「有载体蛋白」与「有能量」，方向始终逆浓度。: The assessment has no new conclusion: active transport needs both "carrier proteins" and "energy", and always goes against the gradient.
供能断开：泵停了，只剩顺浓度的漏: Energy cut: the pump stops, leaving only leakage down the gradient
让 K⁺ 逆浓度进入: Move K⁺ in against the gradient
下列物质中，能以自由扩散方式进出细胞的是: Which of these substances can enter and leave cells by simple diffusion?
氧和二氧化碳很容易自由地通过细胞膜的磷脂双分子层（p.66）。: Oxygen and carbon dioxide pass very easily and freely through the phospholipid bilayer of the cell membrane (p.66).
葡萄糖进入红细胞的方式是: Glucose enters red blood cells by
人红细胞中 K⁺ 的浓度比血浆高 30 倍，K⁺ 仍能进入红细胞，方式是: The K⁺ concentration in human red blood cells is 30 times higher than in plasma, yet K⁺ still enters them. The mode is
逆浓度梯度运输、需要载体蛋白和能量，属于主动运输（p.69）。: Transport against the concentration gradient that needs carrier proteins and energy is active transport (p.69).
细胞把蛋白质（如胃蛋白酶原）运出细胞的方式是: Cells move proteins (such as pepsinogen) out of the cell by
大分子先在细胞内形成囊泡，囊泡与细胞膜融合把大分子排出，即胞吐（p.71、p.7: The large molecule is first packed into a vesicle inside the cell, and the vesicle fuses with the cell membrane to release it: exocytosis (p.71, p.72 exercise 3).
看懂四种跨膜运输方式：顺不顺浓度、要不要蛋白、要不要能量。: Understand the four modes of membrane transport: down the gradient or not, protein or not, energy or not.
示意声明：细胞放大约 4000 倍、细胞膜与囊泡为示意放大；浓度为相对标度（细胞: Disclaimer: the cell is magnified about 4000×, and the membrane and vesicles are schematic close-ups; concentrations are on a relative scale (inside = 100), and net fluxes and per-substance coefficients are lesson settings for comparison only, not measured rates.
